digest.component_or_area: acceptance criteria classification and completion verification
propositions: The canonical AC qualifier `[operator-attested]` must be renamed to `[non-codebase]` to correctly signal WHERE evidence lives rather than WHO attests it, while retaining the old name as an undocumented but permanent backward-compatibility alias to avoid reclassifying 827 immutable event-sourced tickets.

The canonical regex matcher must be widened to accept both `[non-codebase]` and `[operator-attested]` case-insensitively via a non-capturing alternation, ensuring `findall()` arity is unchanged and the alias works identically.

The completion-verdict `kind` wire value must transition from `"operator-attested"` to `"non-codebase"` with reader-widening (audit/page.py) sequenced before emitter changes (contracts.py, schema, prompts) so legacy persisted verdicts render correctly.

The `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` activation trigger and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` classification vocabulary must both be widened to recognize both tag spellings, ensuring `project.measurement-provenance` fires and AC classification works for both forms.

All author-facing guidance (writing-a-passing-plan.md, coach_moves.py move 14, prompts) and the generated criteria guide must emit `[non-codebase]` exclusively, with `[operator-attested]` appearing nowhere in documented surfaces.

The deterministic matcher and LLM-emitted classifications must remain in lockstep by updating prompts and contract digests in a single commit and regenerating the criteria guide with all parity checks.
